To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the olfactory bulb spatial EEG amplitude patterns that are associated with the sniff response are odor specific and are not simply reflections of the olfactory stimulus, (2) nonassociative olfactory learning (habituation) does not produce a permanent change in the spatial EEG patterns, and (3) associative olfactory learning (conditioning) produces coexisting, odor specific spatial EEG amplitude patterns.
the acquisition and retention of olfactory learning are associated with spatial EEG pattern changes in the olfactory bulb.

spatially distributed EEG activity in the olfactory bulb of the rabbit correlates with odor-specific behavior, and that the olfactory bulb EEG patterns change in a manner that is related to the acquisition of differential odor-specific behavioral responding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural basis of olfactory learning.
the relationship between spatial bulbar EEG patterns, olfactory bulb activity patterns in single neurons, and odor-specific sniff behavior.
the relationship between spatial bulbar activity and behavior in olfactory learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

spatial EEG patterns are a correlate of the behavioral state of the olfactory bulb and that the patterns are not simply a reflection of the peripheral olfactory stimulus, and that the patterns change with the acquisition of behavioral learning.

the olfactory bulbar EEG is a reliable index of odor-specific behavior and that the EEG changes observed in these experiments are not simply the result of the odor stimulus but are a reflection of the animal's behavior.
the spatial EEG patterns in the olfactory bulb are a function of the animal's behavior in the presence of the stimulus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
olfactory bulbar EEG spatial patterns are not odor specific, but rather, are stimulus (behavioral response) specific.
spatial EEG amplitude patterns are correlated with odor-specific behavioral response and that the EEG patterns are not simply reflections of the olfactory input.
the olfactory bulb spatially codes odor information and that this spatial coding is modified by nonassociative and by associative learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
olfactory bulbar EEG patterns are not simply odor-specific but are odor-specific and behavior-specific, and that the spatial EEG correlates of odor-specific learning can be measured in the rabbit.
spatial EEG amplitude patterns are sensitive to odor-specific learning, and that the patterns are not simply a reflection of the peripheral stimulation.

the spatial EEG patterns are not a function of peripheral stimulation, that the spatial bulbar EEG patterns change during the habituation of the sniff response, and that coexisting, spatial EEG patterns emerge with the learning of differential behavioral responses.
